articles.title: What in the World - Is ‘ferritin face’ a real thing? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: And what are the signs your iron is low?
articles.body:
World Service , · 05 Nov 2026 , · 8 mins

You might’ve seen lots of chat online about ‘ferritin face’ alongside zoomed in before and after pics of people’s faces. Some claim that changes in their appearance, like pale skin and hair loss, are down to having low ferritin levels. But what even is ferritin? It’s the protein responsible for storing iron in the body. Iron is important for creating red blood cells, which carry oxygen around the body. It’s needed for things like your energy levels, skin and hair health. So, can you tell if your ferritin levels are low just by your face? We break it down with the BBC’s Zara Salaria and Dr Aziza Sesay, who specialises in female health. articles.title: Binance e agora banco francês: como hackers desviaram tanto dinheiro? Entenda as diferenças entre os casos | G1
articles.standfirst: Corretora perdeu US$ 6,3 bilhões em criptomoedas; banco francês teve desvio estimado em 100 milhões de euros. Especialista explica os caminhos usados pelos invasores e como a IA pode ampliar a atuação dos criminosos.
articles.summary: Corretora perdeu US$ 6,3 bilhões em criptomoedas; banco francês teve desvio estimado em 100 milhões de euros. Especialista explica os caminhos usados pelos invasores e como a IA pode ampliar a atuação dos criminosos.
articles.body:
A Binance, maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo, e o banco francês Crédit Mutuel Arkéa foram alvos de ataques hackers em um intervalo de quase uma semana. Os criminosos desviaram bilhões de reais, mas usaram caminhos diferentes para acessar os recursos.

Na Binance, o roubo foi de US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões) . Segundo especialistas, foi o maior roubo de criptomoedas já registrado .

Já o Crédit Mutuel Arkéa informou, na noite desta quarta-feira (4), que sofreu um ataque com desvio estimado em 100 milhões de euros (R$ 615 milhões) .

"No caso da Binance, o roubo foi das próprias carteiras de criptomoedas. Já no caso do banco francês, foram roubados recursos financeiros da instituição, que rapidamente foram convertidos em criptomoedas", explica ao g1 Arthur Igreja, especialista em tecnologia e inovação. Segundo ele, a conversão para cripto facilita a transferência dos valores entre países.

Os dois casos ainda ocorrem em meio a uma onda de ciberataques que também afeta sistemas de refrigeração de supermercados na Suécia, Irlanda, Holanda, Estônia, Finlândia, Bélgica e Luxemburgo.

Logotipo da Binance. — Foto: Dado Ruvic/Reuters

Na Binance, a invasão do notebook de um dos engenheiros pode ter aberto caminho para o roubo . Segundo a corretora, uma investigação inicial indica que o computador pode ter sido usado para acessar um de seus sistemas e fazer saques não autorizados.

"Nossa equipe de segurança está rastreando todo o caminho do ataque através do computador comprometido, que pode ser o ponto de entrada do incidente", afirmou a Binance. Mais tarde, a empresa informou ter identificado outros pontos de invasão.

Mark Karpeles, ex-chefe da corretora de bitcoin Mt Gox, disse à agência de notícias Reuters que os invasores provavelmente acessaram as chaves privadas de pelo menos duas carteiras da Binance. "A Binance parece ter dividido seus ativos em vários sistemas, garantindo que um ataque só possa afetar parte dos ativos, mas mesmo assim um único ataque é uma grande perda", afirmou Karpeles.

A Mt Gox, sediada em Tóquio, encerrou suas atividades há 12 anos, após o roubo de US$ 500 milhões em bitcoin.

Segundo a agência de notícias AFP, a TRM Labs, empresa de análise de blockchain, afirmou ter "alta confiança" de que o ataque foi realizado pelo TraderTraitor, um grupo de hackers ligado à Coreia do Norte. A empresa citou "informações robustas dentro e fora da blockchain".

O Crédit Mutuel Arkéa afirmou que os hackers invadiram seus sistemas e fizeram transferências para outros bancos. Segundo a instituição, as contas dos clientes não foram invadidas, e eles não tiveram prejuízo. O dinheiro roubado foi convertido em criptomoedas.

De acordo com o jornal francês Le Monde, parte dos recursos foi enviada ao banco Kraken, que emitiu um alerta de transação suspeita na terça-feira (3), após receber transferências de valores elevados destinadas a um banco da Europa.

O Crédit Mutuel Arkéa não confirmou o prejuízo de US$ 133 milhões divulgado pelo jornal Le Télégramme, mas indicou que os recursos comprometidos eram dessa ordem.

O especialista Arthur Igreja afirma que os hackers estão se especializando e que ferramentas de inteligência artificial podem ampliar a atuação desses criminosos. Ainda não se sabe, porém, se a IA foi usada nos ataques à Binance e ao banco francês .

"Já existe, há algum tempo, um alerta de que as ferramentas e os modelos de IA poderiam potencializar a atuação desses criminosos. Ela pode ser utilizada para encontrar fragilidades, automatizar tarefas e até aumentar a velocidade da execução de determinadas etapas de um ataque".

O especialista ressalta que, nesse cenário, a IA é uma ferramenta usada pelos hackers. Isso não significa que a tecnologia tenha realizado o ataque por conta própria ou saído de controle.

Igreja também destaca que esses crimes podem ser cometidos à distância, de qualquer lugar do mundo. "Isso também é muito grave, porque pode ser um hacker que está na Coreia do Norte, por exemplo, atacando a Binance. A grande questão é que, onde houver uma fragilidade, muito possivelmente ela será explorada", afirma.

articles.title: Concurso IBGE: 300 vagas na Zona da Mata e Campo das Vertentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira a lista de cidades da Zona da Mata e Campo das Vertentes e quantidade de vagas ofertadas em cada uma delas.
articles.summary: O concurso IBGE abre inscrições para 309 vagas de recenseador na Zona da Mata e Campo das Vertentes, com salários de até R$ 4.370 e exigência de nível fundamental.
articles.body:
309 vagas são reservadas para a Zona da Mata e Campo das Vertentes — Foto: Pexels

Começa nesta sexta-feira (6) e vão até o dia 25 de novembro as inscrições para o processo seletivo simplificado de contratação temporária de recenseadores do 12º Censo Agropecuário, Florestal e Aquícola do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

Ao todo, são ofertadas 27.279 vagas no país, sendo 309 em cidades da Zona da Mata e do Campo das Vertentes . A seguir, confira a lista de municípios das regiões.

Podem se inscrever pessoas que tenham o ensino fundamental completo e mais de 18 anos no momento da contratação. A jornada de trabalho é de 40 horas semanais, e o salário varia entre R$ 1.741 e R$ 4.370 . Entre os benefícios, estão auxílio-alimentação e vale-transporte .

Para se inscrever, o interessado deve acessar o site da comissão organizadora pela internet. É cobrada uma taxa de inscrição no valor de R$ 70 , mas pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade econômica e doadores de medula óssea podem solicitar gratuidade .

Os inscritos deverão fazer prova de conhecimentos sobre matemática, português e habilidades técnicas. A aplicação da prova está prevista para o dia 31 de janeiro de 2027.

articles.title: Falésia desmorona na praia de Pipa, em Tibau do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Deslizamento foi registrado nesta quinta-feira (5), sem feridos, segundo a prefeitura.
articles.summary: Deslizamento na Praia do Madeiro não deixou feridos. Em 2020, queda de falésia na Praia de Pipa matou casal, bebê de sete meses e cachorro.
articles.body:
Um trecho de falésia deslizou na Praia do Madeiro, em Tibau do Sul , no litoral Sul do Rio Grande do Norte, nesta quinta-feira (5). Segundo a prefeitura, não houve registro de pessoas feridas.

Em nota, o município alertou moradores, turistas e frequentadores sobre os riscos de permanecer perto das encostas. A orientação é manter distância segura tanto da base quanto do topo das falésias.

A prefeitura afirmou ainda que "deslizamentos são processos naturais nesse tipo de formação geológica, que pode sofrer erosão e desprendimento de materiais".

O município de Tibau do Sul registrou pelo menos outros dois deslizamentos de falésias em 2026. Em abril, um deslizamento também na praia do Madeiro derrubou árvores e destruiu pelo menos quatro barracas na faixa de areia . Ninguém ficou ferido.

Já em julho, outro trecho de falésia desmoronou, após dois dias de chuvas persistentes na região. Também não houve feridos.

Tragédia em 2020 matou casal e bebê em Pipa

Parte de falésia desabou e deixou 3 mortos de uma mesma família em Pipa, em 2020 — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

As vítimas foram identificadas como Hugo Mendes Pereira, de 32 anos, natural de Jundiaí (SP); Stela Silva de Souza, de 33 anos, natural de Natal; e o filho do casal, Sol. A família estava na faixa de areia, próxima à falésia, quando parte da estrutura desmoronou sobre eles.

Na ocasião, testemunhas relataram que a mãe tentou proteger o bebê com um abraço. O menino chegou a ser encontrado com vida, mas uma médica que estava na praia tentou reanimá-lo e não conseguiu.

O acidente aconteceu na Praia do Centro, na região da Baía dos Golfinhos, em Pipa. Na época, moradores relataram que a ação do mar desgastava a base das falésias e aumentava o risco de desabamentos.

Falésia desliza na Praia do Madeiro, em Tibau do Sul — Foto: Reprodução / Tibau Notícias Pipa

articles.title: Poços artesianos no Amazonas: como regularizar e evitar multas | G1
articles.standfirst: Instituto de Proteção Ambiental do Amazonas (Ipaam) é responsável pelas autorizações. Quem descumprir as regras pode receber multas de até R$ 100 mil, além de ter o poço embargado.
articles.summary: Poços artesianos no Amazonas exigem licença do Ipaam para evitar multas de R$ 100 mil; confira taxas, prazos e como obter a outorga de uso da água.
articles.body:
Poços tubulares precisam de autorização no Amazonas — Foto: Divulgação/Ipaam

Quem pretende perfurar um poço tubular no Amazonas precisa de autorização do Instituto de Proteção Ambiental do Amazonas (Ipaam) antes de iniciar a obra. Além disso, para retirar e utilizar a água, é necessário obter uma outorga de direito de uso de recursos hídricos, exceto nos casos previstos na legislação. O uso irregular pode gerar multas de R$ 100 a R$ 100 mil , além de outras penalidades.

Entre maio e outubro de 2026, o Ipaam registrou 209 pedidos de outorga e dispensas no Cadastro Nacional de Usuários de Recursos Hídricos (CNARH). Manaus concentrou a maior parte dos registros, com 164. Em seguida aparecem Apuí , com sete, e Canutama , com cinco.

A regularização permite acompanhar a quantidade de água retirada dos mananciais e identificar possíveis problemas, como o uso excessivo e a contaminação. O controle também ajuda a proteger as fontes de abastecimento.

A autorização para perfurar o poço e a permissão para utilizar a água são documentos diferentes.

Antes de iniciar a obra, o interessado precisa solicitar ao Ipaam a Licença Ambiental Única (LAU), que autoriza a perfuração do poço tubular.

Depois, para retirar e utilizar a água, é necessário obter a outorga de direito de uso de recursos hídricos ou verificar se a atividade se enquadra em alguma das situações de dispensa previstas na legislação.

A outorga estabelece a quantidade de água que pode ser retirada, a finalidade do uso e o período de validade da autorização.

A exigência vale para estabelecimentos comerciais, condomínios, indústrias e produtores rurais que utilizam água diretamente de poços, rios, lagos e igarapés.

Quem recebe água exclusivamente da rede pública de abastecimento não precisa solicitar uma outorga individual. Nesse caso, a regularização da captação é responsabilidade da empresa ou do órgão que presta o serviço.

A legislação prevê algumas situações de dispensa. Uma delas é a retirada de até 5 mil litros de água por dia, por domicílio, para uso doméstico em pequenos núcleos rurais.

A regra vale para comunidades com até 51 residências ou 400 habitantes, desde que sejam atendidas as demais condições estabelecidas pela Resolução nº 02/2016 do Conselho Estadual de Recursos Hídricos do Amazonas (CERH-AM).

Para solicitar a outorga, o interessado precisa pagar uma taxa administrativa de R$ 20,49 , referente à Guia de Expediente.

Já o custo da Licença Ambiental Única (LAU), necessária para perfurar o poço, varia conforme o porte da estrutura:

A licença tem validade de 30 dias . Além das taxas, o interessado pode ter gastos com estudos, análises da água e outros documentos técnicos exigidos pelo órgão ambiental.

O pedido deve ser feito pelo site do Ipaam. Confira o caminho:

Acesse o site do Ipaam ( ipaam.am.gov.br );

Selecione Outorga de Recursos Hídricos ;

Clique em Outorga de Captação de Águas Subterrâneas ;

Consulte os formulários e a lista de documentos necessários.

A documentação varia conforme a finalidade do uso da água e pode incluir informações sobre o local, a quantidade de água utilizada e as características do poço.

Quais são as penalidades para quem utiliza poços irregulares?

A fiscalização do Ipaam verifica se os poços possuem as autorizações exigidas e se a quantidade de água retirada respeita os limites estabelecidos.

Entre as irregularidades estão perfurar um poço sem licença, utilizar água sem outorga quando ela é obrigatória e retirar um volume maior do que o permitido.

De acordo com a Lei Estadual nº 3.167/2007, os responsáveis podem receber advertências e multas de R$ 100 a R$ 100 mil. Dependendo da gravidade da infração, também podem ocorrer a suspensão das atividades e o embargo do poço, que impede o uso até a regularização.

Em caso de dúvidas sobre documentos, taxas e procedimentos, a Gerência de Recursos Hídricos (GERH) do Ipaam atende pelo telefone (92) 2123-6734 .

articles.title: Homem da Meia-Noite tem traz temática sertaneja para desfile de 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Josildo Sá, Cristina Amaral, Terezinha do Acordeon, Assisão são homenageados pelo Calunga no desfile nas ladeiras do Sítio Histórico de Olinda na madrugada entre 5 e 6 de fevereiro.
articles.summary: Tema do desfile faz referência à essência do interior de Pernambuco. Josildo Sá, Cristina Amaral, Terezinha do Acordeon, Assisão e Caretas de Triunfo são os homenageados do bloco.
articles.body:
Homem da Meia-Noite 2027 traz Josildo Sá, Cristina Amaral, Terezinha do Acordeon, Assisão e Caretas de Triunfo como homenageados — Foto: Clara Oliveira/g1

No carnaval de 2027, o Homem da Meia-Noite desfila pelas ladeiras de Olinda com o tema “SERtão”, reverenciando o Sertão do Pajeú de Pernambuco e as pessoas que fazem a cultura no interior do estado. Os homenageados são Josildo Sá, Cristina Amaral, Terezinha do Acordeon, Assisão e Caretas de Triunfo ( saiba mais abaixo sobre eles ).

O desfile do calunga acontece à meia-noite, entre os dias 5 e 6 de fevereiro de 2027, no Largo do Bonsucesso. O tema escolhido busca exaltar a essência, a resistência e a memória do povo sertanejo de Pernambuco e tem como lema “O gigante de Olinda, o frevo e o Pajeú”, unindo a simplicidade do Sertão pernambucano com a grandeza cultural do Carnaval e do estado.

“Uma grandeza que não se mede pelo que se possui, mas por aquilo que se carrega na alma. É uma riqueza que nasce da terra, floresce na cultura e se revela nas pessoas. Gente que transforma a simplicidade em grandeza, a dificuldade em resistência e a memória em herança. E é essa riqueza humana que o Homem da Meia-Noite escolhe celebrar: um olhar para nossas origens, para a nossa identidade e para aquilo que verdadeiramente nos constitui. Porque, antes de qualquer conquista existe o ser, antes do ter existe a essência, antes de tudo existe aquilo que somos”, disse o presidente do Homem da Meia-Noite, Luiz Adolpho.

Josildo Sá : natural de Floresta , o cantor e compositor de músicas como “Noite de Forrobodó” e “Pra virar lobisomem” se consagrou, em mais de 20 anos de carreira, pelo samba de latada e pelo forró;

Cristina Amaral : a cantora, nascida em Sertânia , é reconhecida pela sua atuação no carnaval de Pernambuco ao longo de décadas;

Terezinha do Acordeon : a cantora e instrumentista natural de Salgueiro começou a tocar sanfona aos 14 anos e tem, entre os sucessos, canções omo “Forró de dois” e “No Forró do bole-bole”.

Assisão : o sanfoneiro nascido em Serra Talhada , considerado patrimônio vivo de Pernambuco, compôs, em 64 anos de carreira, clássicos do forró, como “Fogueirinha” e “Eu quero meu amor”.

Caretas de Triunfo : mascarados que fazem parte do carnaval desse município sertanejo desse 1917 e são patrimônio cultural, misturando o carnaval com o reisado, uma das manifestações folclóricas e religiosas mais tradicionais do Nordeste.

Ramylle Barbosa mostra a cartola do Homem da Meia-Noite, que faz referência ao artesanato de couro de Pernambuco — Foto: Clara Oliveira/g1

A estilista Ramylle Barbosa é responsável pela confecção do traje do Homem da Meia-Noite. Ela, que também é brincante dos Caretas de Triunfo, contou que a principal inspiração para o figurino do calunga foi o artesanato de couro do interior de Pernambuco.

"A [roupa] é relacionada à nossa cultura do couro, aos celeiros de Pernambuco e às pessoas que trabalham com a arte do couro. E, para a cartola do Homem da Meia-Noite, a gente trouxe esse trabalho manual e o detalhe do barbicacho, o encaixe para o chapéu não cair da cabeça nas cavalgadas, para levar o sentimento sertanejo para a roupa", disse Ramylle Barbosa.

Em 2026, o Homem da Meia-Noite desfilou com o tema “Tambores Silenciosos” , fazendo tributo à ancestralidade afro-brasileira e homenageando nomes como a Mãe Beth de Oxum, Siba, Maciel Salú, Grupo Bongar e o Maracatu Nação Pernambuco.

articles.title: MP relata mudança de versões sobre morte de tatuador em Nuporanga, SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Criança contou que foi abordada por Vitor Fonseca porque estava sozinha e ele disse que a acompanharia até a praça onde a irmã dela estava. MP diz que réu e amigos mudaram versões no depoimento.
articles.summary: Criança contou que foi abordada por Vitor Fonseca porque estava sozinha e ele disse que a acompanharia até a praça onde a irmã dela estava.
articles.body:
Além de versões diferentes nos depoimentos do réu, Vitor Manoel, de 25, e das pessoas que estavam com ele, a professora da menina de 8 anos que aparece nas imagens ao lado de Fonseca diz que ouviu da própria criança que o tatuador 'não mexeu com ela', como chegou a afirmar o agressor.

Segundo a menina disse à professora, Fonseca se aproximou dela para perguntar porque ela estava sozinha, uma vez que já era madrugada, e ao que ela disse que estava indo encontrar a irmã em uma praça, ele afirmou que a acompanharia.

Fonseca morreu dois dias depois de levar um soco de Manoel no meio de uma praça na cidade. O caso aconteceu na madrugada do dia 15 de fevereiro.

À época, Manoel chegou a dizer que agiu motivado por uma suposta importunação por parte de Fonseca a menores , o que não se confirmou. Ele é réu no processo que investiga o caso e responde por lesão corporal seguida de morte .

Após levar o soco, o tatuador caiu desacordado e bateu a cabeça no solo. O laudo necroscópico apontou que ele morreu em decorrência de um traumatismo craniano.

A EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, procurou a defesa de Manoel, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Vitor Manoel, de 25 anos, foi acusado por causar morte de tatuador com agressão no carnaval de Nuporanga, SP. — Foto: Reprodução/ Câmeras de segurança

Segundo o Ministério Público, o irmão de Manoel deu duas versões sobre o caso: primeiro, dizendo que Fonseca os seguia e que ele e o grupo chegaram a alterar o caminho para confirmar a perseguição, e depois disse que considerou a atitude do tatuador normal.

A esposa de Manoel também mudou a versão: aos policiais disse que, ao ser afastado, o tatuador disse à criança para acompanhá-lo e isso teria despertado a fúria do marido, que agrediu Fonseca.

Depois, em juízo, ela disse que o tatuador puxou a menina e que, ao mandarem que ele saísse dali, ele não foi. As imagens mostram que é Vitor Manuel quem vai até Fonseca.

À EPTV , o advogado Ricardo Rocha, assistente de acusação do caso, disse que vai usar as contradições no processo.

"Os próprios relatos dos oito que estavam ali envolvidos e parte deles foram ouvidos em juízo já tem contradições entre si, entre o investigado e as pessoas que seriam amigos dele. Além disso, muitas das coisas que eles narram que teria supostamente acontecido, as câmeras desmentem. E o próprio relatório da polícia desmente a versão apresentada por eles. As imagens dizem outra coisa".

Vitor Fonseca de Almeida Silva morreu após ser agredido durante o carnaval em Nuporanga, SP — Foto: Redes sociais

articles.title: Tempestades no Vale do Paraíba e litoral: Defesa Civil dá alerta | G1
articles.standfirst: Frente fria avança sobre o estado e, em contato com o calor, pode provocar temporais com ventos de até 80 km/h, raios e queda de granizo.
articles.summary: Tempestades no Vale do Paraíba e litoral de SP podem ter ventos de 80 km/h e granizo; Defesa Civil alerta para riscos de alagamentos e deslizamentos até sábado.
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo emitiu um alerta laranja para a ocorrência de tempestades entre esta quinta-feira (5) e sábado (7). A previsão inclui chuva forte, rajadas de vento e possibilidade de queda de granizo.

A mudança no tempo já começou a ser sentida em cidades do Vale do Paraíba e região. Na noite de quarta-feira (4), houve registros de raios e chuva localizada em alguns municípios.

A instabilidade é provocada pela passagem de uma frente fria que avança pelo Sul do país. Apesar da mudança, o calor deve continuar até sábado (7). O encontro entre as altas temperaturas e a frente fria pode favorecer a formação de temporais.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, os ventos podem chegar a 80 km/h em algumas regiões do estado, como na divisa com o Paraná, no litoral paulista, na capital e na Grande São Paulo.

"Em caso de emergência, nós colocaremos o time na rua para o atendimento das ocorrências. Jamais atravesse ruas alagadas, gente. Uma lâmina de água cobrindo a calçada já é suficiente para arrastar o seu carro ou para te derrubar e te arrastar", disse o capitão da Defesa Civil de SP Maxwel Souza.

Diante da previsão, o órgão mobilizou o gabinete de crise, que está ativado em modalidade remota. As concessionárias de serviços públicos também estão em prontidão para atender possíveis ocorrências.

Defesa Civil alerta que até mesmo uma lâmina de água sobre a rua pode ser suficiente para arrastar veículos e pessoas durante temporais. — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Vanguarda/Arquivo

A Defesa Civil orienta a população a evitar atravessar ruas alagadas, mesmo quando a quantidade de água parece pequena. Uma lâmina de água pode ser suficiente para arrastar veículos e pessoas.

Outra recomendação é manter distância de árvores, que podem cair durante as rajadas de vento.

Moradores de áreas de risco também devem ficar atentos aos sinais de possíveis deslizamentos de terra, como rachaduras nas paredes das casas e portas e janelas que começam a apresentar dificuldade para abrir ou fechar. Esses sinais podem indicar movimentação do solo.

articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada nessa quarta-feira (4), em Sena Madureira. Bombeiros conseguiram combater o fogo e impedir que chamas atingissem residências próximas ao local.
articles.summary: Ocorrência foi registrada nessa quarta-feira (4), em Sena Madureira. Bombeiros conseguiram combater o fogo e impedir que chamas atingissem residências próximas ao local.
articles.body:
Um incêndio de grandes proporções atingiu uma área de vegetação de, aproximadamente, 9 mil metros quadrados, próximo a uma torre de comunicação na Avenida Brasil, no município de Sena Madureira , no interior do Acre, nessa quarta-feira (4). Ninguém se feriu.

Um vídeo mostra a área atingida pelo fogo e o trabalho do Corpo de Bombeiros no combate ao incêndio. Nas imagens, é possível ver a fumaça no local e as chamas remanescentes na área. ( Veja o vídeo acima )

Segundo informações do Corpo de Bombeiros, as chamas se propagaram e ameaçavam residências próximas à região.

Incêndio atinge área próxima a torre de comunicação no Acre — Foto: Marcio Farias/Arquivo pessoal

Ao chegar ao local, a equipe iniciou o combate ao fogo que durou cerca de três horas. O incêndio, segundo os militares, foi controlado e extinto.

Ainda de acordo com os bombeiros, também foram feitas ações de proteção às residências próximas para evitar que as chamas atingissem os imóveis.

articles.title: Irmã de Marília Mendonça revela fotos da infância e cita fenômeno | G1
articles.standfirst: Laura Mendonça é irmã de Marília Mendonça por parte de pai. Além de fotos, ela compartilhou algumas histórias sobre como era ser irmã da Rainha da Sofrência.
articles.summary: Laura Mendonça é irmã de Marília Mendonça por parte de pai. Além de fotos, ela compartilhou algumas histórias sobre como era ser irmã da Rainha da Sofrência.
articles.body:
A irmã de Marília Mendonça revelou algumas fotos da infância com a cantora em entrevista à TV Anhanguera, que exibe uma série especial no aniversário da morte da cantora , que completou cinco anos (veja o vídeo acima) . Laura Mendonça relembrou momentos com Marília e destacou que nem mesmo a família conseguia entender o tamanho da estrela que ela havia se tornado.

"Ela é minha irmã. Uma irmã que estourou, despontou, virou um fenômeno e nem a gente tinha ideia do tamanho que era, de tudo o que a Marília construiu e fez em tão pouco tempo de carreira, tão nova. Ela deixou um legado muito grande", disse ela.

Nas fotos, Marília aparece ainda bem pequena, mas já é possível reconhecer os traços inconfundíveis da cantora que encantou o Brasil .

Irmã de Marília Mendonça revela fotos da infância da cantora e cita fenômeno: 'A gente não tinha ideia do tamanho que era' — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

Laura conta que ela e Marília são irmãs por parte de pai e explica a árvore genealógica da família. São quatro filhos do primeiro casamento, três do segundo, Marília do terceiro, com dona Ruth, e o filho caçula do quarto casamento.

Fotos de Marília Mendonça na infância — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

Mesmo sendo filhas de mães diferentes, as duas eram próximas. Laura conta que quando viu Marília pela primeira vez, ela estava "toda arrumadinha", vestida de rosa. Bem humorada, ela aproveitou para contar uma situação engraçada entre as irmãs.

"Chega a Marília com dois diademas prendendo o cabelo, uma rasteirinha, uma saiona... Eu falei 'Que marmota é essa? Você vai falar para mim que estava em uma reunião de negócios, você não foi desse jeito não, né?", disse ela, que lembra das risadas da irmã ao ouvir o comentário.

Laura conta que não sente revolta pela partida da irmã e acredita que o que aconteceu foi um propósito de Deus. Segundo ela, os fãs da cantora enviam mensagens a ela todos os dias. "Sabe o que eu falo para eles? 'Se você tivesse tido a oportunidade de ter conhecido ela pessoalmente, você seria muito mais fã. Porque Marília era gente'" .

Marília Mendonça na infância — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

No dia 5 de novembro de 2021, Marília Mendonça morreu aos 26 anos, no auge da carreira. A cantora embarcou em um voo que partiu de Goiânia com destino a Minas Gerais, onde realizaria um show na cidade mineira de Caratinga.

A aeronave caiu em uma área rural e ninguém sobreviveu à queda. Além da artista, do piloto e do copiloto, também estavam no avião o tio de Marília, Abicieli Silveira Dias Filho, de 43 anos, e o seu produtor, Henrique Ribeiro, de 32 anos.

Cantora Marília Mendonça — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram Marília Mendonça

A cantora permanece como uma das artistas mais escutadas do país mesmo após cinco anos da sua partida. Marília é considerada por músicos e especialistas a líder de um movimento que colocou as mulheres como protagonistas da música sertaneja.

articles.title: Ten years of the Paris Agreement: Has the world kept its climate promises?
articles.summary: Nearly 200 countries pledged to limit warming to 1.5C. We look at who has delivered and who has fallen short.
articles.body:
Ten years ago, the Paris Agreement entered into force, binding nearly every country to a shared goal: to hold global warming well below 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit) above preindustrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5C (2.7F).

A decade on, the deal has helped drive stronger climate policies and a rapid expansion of clean energy. But emissions remain near record highs, temperatures keep climbing and countries are still far from the cuts needed to keep a 1.5C limit within reach.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera looks at what the Paris Agreement set out to do, how far global temperatures have risen since and which countries are driving emissions.

The Paris Agreement is a legally binding climate treaty adopted by 196 parties at the United Nations climate summit in Paris, also known as COP21, on December 12, 2015. It entered into force on November 4, 2016.

The United States, the world’s second-largest greenhouse gas emitter after China, has joined and left the agreement twice. President Donald Trump ordered both withdrawals. The first took effect in November 2020, and President Joe Biden rejoined in February 2021. The US left again in January this year, 12 months after Trump ordered its exit for a second time.

Today, 194 parties, 193 countries and the European Union, belong to the agreement.

Rather than imposing the same cuts on everyone, the agreement asks each government to set its own targets through nationally determined contributions, or NDCs, outlining how it will cut emissions and adapt to climate change.

Countries submit a new, more ambitious NDC every five years, and a Global Stocktake assesses collective progress on the same cycle. The agreement also covers reporting, climate finance and support for developing countries.

The agreement does not force countries to meet their targets. It relies on transparency and international pressure to raise ambition.

How close is the world to breaking the 1.5C limit?

Temperatures have kept rising since the deal was adopted.

In 2024, the planet was more than 1.5C warmer than preindustrial levels across a full calendar year for the first time.

The past three years, 2023 to 2025, were the hottest on record and the first three-year period to average more than 1.5C of warming.

The long-term warming average now stands at about 1.4C, and scientists expect it to surpass 1.5C around the end of this decade.

In October, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said the chance of keeping warming to 1.5C without overshooting it has been lost.

“Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5C increases climate impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year,” UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen said.

Still, the outlook is less bleak than it was in 2015.

When the Paris Agreement was signed, existing policies put the world on course for about 3.6C of warming by 2100. According to the Climate Action Tracker , that projection has since fallen to about 2.6C as countries adopted climate policies and clean energy expanded.

Progress has stalled since 2021, however, and current policies still point to far more warming than the agreement promised.

Carbon dioxide, the main driver of warming, comes mostly from burning coal, oil and natural gas while deforestation removes trees that once absorbed it.

China, the US and India now produce more than half of the world’s annual emissions. China alone emits more than the US, India, Russia and Japan combined although the US has released the most carbon emissions historically.

Investments in clean energy are now almost double those in fossil fuels, but emission cuts have been too slow to keep 1.5C within reach.

The graphic below ranks the biggest emitters in 2024 and shows how their emissions have changed since the agreement took effect in 2016.

China remains by far the largest polluter, and its emissions have kept rising alongside those of India and Indonesia as these fast-growing economies burn more coal to meet soaring power demand. Indonesia has climbed into the top 10, replacing Canada.

Germany, Japan and the US have cut their emissions, largely by replacing coal with renewables and gas. But growth elsewhere has outweighed those cuts, and global emissions are 9 percent higher than in 2016.

articles.title: South Korea plans to expand anti-piracy operations closer to Hormuz Strait
articles.summary: Seoul proposes extending its Cheonghae unit’s patrols to waters near Oman’s Duqm amid US pressure over Iran war.
articles.body:
South Korea plans to expand its anti-piracy patrols off the coast of Somalia to waters closer to the Strait of Hormuz, the Ministry of National Defense said, following pressure from the United States to provide support for the war on Iran.

The government will ask the National Assembly to extend the mandate of the Cheonghae unit, a naval task force due to expire at the end of 2026, a Defence Ministry spokesperson told the Reuters news agency on Thursday. The request would also widen the unit’s area of operations to waters near the port of Duqm in Oman, about 650km (403 miles) from the Strait of Hormuz.

The motion will go to lawmakers after the cabinet endorses it next week, the Yonhap news agency reported.

The Cheonghae unit has patrolled the Gulf of Aden since 2009 to protect commercial shipping. Its latest contingent sailed from South Korea’s Busan on October 2 on board the Chungmugong Yi Sun-sin, a 4,400-tonne destroyer carrying a maritime helicopter and about 300 service members.

Under the new mandate, the unit would push northeast into the Arabian Sea south of Oman, roughly doubling its operating radius to about 1,930km (1,200 miles), officials told Yonhap.

It would add 75 personnel, including a bomb disposal team, and a P-8A maritime patrol aircraft to help monitor shipping routes.

Officials told Yonhap the mission would be strictly noncombat and the unit would remain under South Korean command, operating independently of allied forces.

“The enhancement of the Cheonghae unit’s mission is to protect our citizens and safeguard our economic interests,” a defence official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Yonhap.

“Operations will remain restricted to the open waters south of Oman, and the maritime patrol aircraft will be prohibited from targeting or monitoring Iranian territory, territorial waters or the interior of the Strait of Hormuz during their missions,” he said.

The latest proposal follows pressure from US President Donald Trump for Seoul to support Washington’s war on Iran.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung pledged in April to help safeguard shipping during talks led by the United Kingdom and France. In September, he said he would avoid any deployment that could draw South Korea into the war.

Opposition lawmakers have argued against an expansion of the Cheonghae unit’s mission.

“Expanding the Cheonghae unit’s operational area amounts to a troop deployment,” Kim Joon-hyung, the floor leader of the small left-leaning Rebuilding Korea Party, said at a news conference at the National Assembly in Seoul on Wednesday.

“It is not a clever solution but a deceptive workaround.”

Kim warned that an expanded mission could expose South Korean forces to Iranian retaliation, even if Seoul insisted that its personnel would not take part in combat.

“If President Donald Trump boasts that South Korea was the first country in the world to dispatch troops, we would become the first country to join the Middle East war,” he said.

articles.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in jail
articles.summary: Wong, in prison since 2020, was found guilty of colluding with foreign entities in violation of national security law.
articles.body:
Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong , who has been in prison since 2020, has been jailed for an additional 10 years.

Hong Kong’s High Court found Wong guilty of colluding with foreign entities in violation of the city’s national security law on Thursday.

The sentence comes just two months before he was expected to be released in January 2027.

“The punishment must fit the gravity of ⁠the crime,” High Court Judge William Tam told a packed courtroom while delivering the sentence.

“It is also necessary for the court to express the community’s abhorrence of the defendant’s scheme and acts with others to collude with foreign forces or external elements to endanger national security.”

Wong, now 30, was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and others to ask foreign countries, bodies or individuals outside China to impose sanctions or blockades, or engage in other hostile activities against the government.

He pleaded guilty to the charge in September. Tam said he considered a 13-year prison sentence as a starting point but reduced it to 10 because of Wong’s guilty plea and mitigation.

Wong was once the face of Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement and has been in jail since 2020. He was imprisoned over his role in protests held a year earlier.

The demonstrations were prompted by plans to allow extradition to mainland China but soon evolved into a wider pro-democracy movement. Wong became a prominent representative of the movement, regularly appearing on news channels. He later pleaded guilty to inciting and organising an unauthorised antigovernment assembly.

Governments and rights groups criticised the court’s decision on Thursday.

The United States consulate in Hong Kong said that it “strongly condemns” the additional sentence handed to Wong, and called for his “immediate release”.

“Wong has been unjustly imprisoned since December 2020, demonstrating that Beijing will go to extraordinary lengths to silence those who advocate for fundamental freedoms in Hong Kong,” a consulate spokesperson said in a statement to the AFP news agency.

After his sentencing, Taiwan also criticised the “endless political persecution” of Hong Kong pro-democracy activists.

Beijing and the Hong Kong government use “authoritarian tools” to “fabricate charges … engage in endless political persecution, and suppress the people’s legitimate rights to pursue freedom, democracy, and human rights,” Taiwan’s top China policy body said.

Human Rights Watch denounced the latest charge against Wong. “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust. Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars,” said Elaine Pearson, the group’s Asia director.

Amnesty International also criticised Wong’s additional sentence, saying it was “another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent”.

articles.title: Three siblings discover their late father had two children from a secret relationship; court awards £170,000 to two sons, while all five biological children become entitled to shares of his £461,000 estate
articles.summary: Three siblings were shocked to discover that their late father had fathered two children during a decades-long relationship he had kept secret from his
articles.body: Three siblings were shocked to discover that their late father had fathered two children during a decades-long relationship he had kept secret from his wife and their family. The revelation came shortly before his death, leaving the five biological children facing an unexpected inheritance dispute over an estate worth approximately £461,000. As neither parent had made a will, the estate was initially set to be divided equally among all five children under England's intestacy rules. However, two of the three siblings challenged the arrangement, arguing that their father's estate included money inherited from their late mother, who had not known about his other relationship. A court subsequently awarded £170,000 to the two brothers based on their financial needs.How the family discovered their father's secret relationshipThe case involved Michael Gymer, who died in 2020 at the age of 83, just months after his wife, Julie, who was 81. The couple had three children together: Shelley, Gregory and Lee.Shortly before Michael's death, the three siblings discovered that their father had maintained a long relationship with another woman, Beverley Madden, and had two children with her: Charlotte and Joseph. The relationship had reportedly continued for decades, with Michael concealing the existence of his second family from Julie and their three children.Charlotte and Joseph were 32 and 29 respectively when the inheritance dispute came to light. The five half-siblings had not previously known about one another.Why all five children were initially entitled to the inheritanceNeither Michael nor Julie had made a will. Under the intestacy rules in England and Wales, Julie's estate passed to her surviving husband when she died. When Michael subsequently died without a will, his estate, including the assets he had inherited from Julie, was initially due to be divided equally among his five biological children.The estate was valued at approximately £461,000, meaning each child was initially set to receive around £92,350.Gregory and Lee challenged this arrangement. They argued that a substantial part of the money had originally belonged to their mother, who had accumulated her share through years of work. They said it was unfair for that money to pass indirectly to Charlotte and Joseph, who were not Julie's children and whom she had not known about.Court rejects claim that their mother knew about the affairCharlotte and Joseph argued that Julie had known about their father's relationship with their mother and had accepted that they could inherit from him.However, the court rejected this argument, finding no convincing evidence that Julie knew about the affair or the existence of the two children. Beverley Madden had reportedly claimed that Julie knew about the relationship, but the judge was not persuaded by her account.The judge described all five children as innocent of their father's deception. The dispute, therefore, was not about whether Charlotte and Joseph were Michael's biological children or whether they were entitled to inherit from him. It centred on whether the original equal division adequately provided for Gregory and Lee, given the circumstances surrounding the money their father had inherited from Julie.Why the court awarded £170,000 to the two brothersGregory and Lee brought their claim under the Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975, which allows eligible people to ask a court to reconsider an estate's distribution if they believe reasonable financial provision has not been made for them.After considering the circumstances and the financial needs of the five children, the judge ordered that £170,000 be returned to Julie's estate and divided between Gregory and Lee. Their sister Shelley did not receive an additional award because the judge found that she did not have the same financial need.The decision meant that the two brothers received additional provision from the money associated with their late mother, while Charlotte and Joseph remained entitled to inherit from their father.How the £461,000 estate was dividedFollowing the ruling, Gregory and Lee were each expected to receive approximately £143,000, including their additional awards of around £85,000. Their sister Shelley, along with their father's two children from the secret relationship, Charlotte and Joseph, were each expected to receive approximately £58,000. This meant all five children retained a share of Michael's estate, but Gregory and Lee received larger portions because of the court's additional provision for their financial needs. articles.title: Florida authorities say 2 dead at Tampa office complex, including gunman shot by security guard
articles.summary: A gunman plowed a car into a courtyard on Citibank’s sprawling Tampa business campus on Wednesday and opened fire with a rifle, killing a woman before a security guard fatally shot him, authorities said.
articles.body: TAMPA, Fla. — A gunman plowed a car into a courtyard on Citibank’s sprawling Tampa business campus on Wednesday and opened fire with a rifle, killing a woman before a security guard fatally shot him, authorities said. The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office did not give a motive for the shooting or say whether the gunman and his lone victim knew each other. The attack sent workers scrambling as the suspect crashed his car among outdoor tables where people were eating lunch, then started shooting, said Chief Deputy Frank Losat of the sheriff’s office. He said 3,200 people were on the campus at work during the attack. The gunman fatally shot the woman before a security guard confronted him in a cafeteria, Losat said. The guard and the gunman exchanged fire, and the guard killed him, Losat said. “Was there a potential for further violence? Absolutely,” Losat told a news conference. “So kudos to that security guard.” The names of the gunman and the woman killed were not immediately released. Losat said four other people were taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. He didn’t know whether any of them had been shot or struck by the gunman’s vehicle. Citibank VP heard ‘incredible clatter’ of gunfire, then screaming The Citibank campus in suburban Tampa includes four three-story office buildings that house thousands of the banking giant’s employees. David Dzien, a Citibank vice president, told The Associated Press he was returning to work after lunch when he saw the shooter’s sedan crash through a fence about 150 yards (137 meters) away from him, followed by an “incredible clatter” that he later realized was gunfire. People near the crashed car suddenly dispersed and others began to scream, Dzien said, as he sprinted back into the building and evacuated through a fire escape. “I can still hear the particular type of scream,” he said, “and I’m still trying to process it, frankly.” The attack occurred on a day when “VIPs” who don’t normally work at the complex were present for a “quarterly review,” Dzien said. More than 360 deputies began arriving immediately Sheriff’s deputies began arriving at the campus within a minute of the first 911 call, Losat said. The response was huge, with more than 360 deputies — many in tactical gear — rushing to the scene. Those deputies spent 2 1/2 hours searching and clearing the building where the shootings occurred plus adjacent office buildings, Losat said. Radio traffic on Broadcastify.com from responding officers described an exhaustive floor-by-floor search as people were found sheltering in locked rooms and closets, then carefully escorted from the buildings and parking garage. Citigroup said in a statement that it was “aware of an incident” at the complex and was cooperating with authorities. Nearby hotel gave shelter to hundreds of fleeing workers Employees at the Sheraton Tampa Brandon Hotel, a few hundred feet from the Citibank complex, were having a monthly employee luncheon in the hotel’s ballroom when they saw a massive flood of police vehicles headed toward the campus. General Manager Matt Chauvin said Citibank employees ran over and told the front desk there was an active shooter. “We at first locked the doors and, you know, went into lockdown, but the employees kept coming over,” Chauvin said. Chauvin estimated the hotel sheltered about 300 Citibank workers. Hotel staff gave them water and lunch, and let some go into hotel rooms “to sort of decompress or make phone calls.” “Luckily we were far enough away that they were all safe,” he said.

articles.title: A still-recovering pope will head home to Latin America and his beloved Peru for a 12-day trip
articles.summary: Three weeks after lung cancer surgery, Pope Leo XIV is embarking on the longest and farthest trip of his pontificate: a 12-day, three-nation tour of Latin America
articles.body: VATICAN CITY — Three weeks after lung cancer surgery, Pope Leo XIV is embarking on the longest and farthest trip of his pontificate: a 12-day, three-nation tour of Latin America that carries more personal and historic weight than any of his voyages to date. The U.S.-born Leo is returning home to Peru, where the former Robert Prevost lived for two decades as a missionary priest and learned to be the pastor he is today. Leo holds Peruvian citizenship and is so attached to Peru’s people he gave them a shoutout in Spanish from the balcony of St. Peter’s Basilica on the night of his election. Leo is also going to Argentina, the home of his predecessor, Pope Francis, to whom Leo owes his pontificate. It will be a homecoming of sorts there, too, since Francis never returned to Argentina after his 2013 election, leaving a complicated legacy that Leo will now have to navigate. Leo starts his trip Friday in Uruguay, the least Catholic, most secular country in all of Latin America, where not even the big Catholic feast days get their due: Christmas in Uruguay is officially “Family Day” and Holy Week is “Tourism Week.” Leo is nevertheless expected to draw huge crowds throughout his trip and will likely raise issues of concern to his still-young pontificate: economic injustice, the plight of Indigenous peoples and the Amazon, and the church’s dreadful legacy of clergy sexual abuse. But many eyes will be on Leo himself for having confirmed this grueling trip at all so soon after surgery Oct. 13 to remove a cancerous tumor from his lung. When doctors announced that Leo required no further treatment, they also said there was no reason why he couldn’t make the Nov. 6-17 trip. It includes a dozen flights and two helicopter rides covering 31,000 kilometers (19,000 miles), the longest of Leo’s pontificate. While popes always travel with ample medical care, the Vatican said no special or additional provisions are planned for Leo, including when the 71-year-old travels to Cusco, Peru, at an altitude of 3,400 meters (11,200 feet). “We’re not talking of a permanent condition,” said Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni. “We’re talking about something that you heal from, because it is surgery.” A papal homecoming to Peru No leg of the trip is more anticipated than the final stop in Peru, with Leo’s arrival in Lima, and after that Chiclayo, his beloved former diocese that he headed from 2015-2023, when Francis summoned him to Rome. “He is so excited. He personally confirmed this trip with no changes,” said Maria Montserrat Alvarado, the Vatican’s new communications chief. Leo told the region’s bishops in September that it was in Peru where he “came to know firsthand the faith of a people from whom I received so much, and I came to understand better what it means to be a shepherd.” Alvarado said Peru “opened his eyes” to the diverse needs of the church and how the church encounters its flock. “This is a place that gave him his ministry and inspired who he is as a pastor,” she said. Alvarado predicted that Leo will speak off-the-cuff in Spanish throughout the visit and will show his true feelings much in the same way he did in June during his visit to Spain, where the world saw a much more relaxed and happy Leo than the reserved, quiet one often on display in Rome. “You will see that again but in a totally different way because he knows these streets,” she said. Another homecoming to Argentina, with a different pope Francis befuddled friends and foes alike for the duration of his 13-year pontificate, because he never returned home. He had plenty of opportunities, including during his first trip as pope to Rio de Janeiro, and subsequent trips to the region, including to neighboring Chile and Bolivia. “How many times, I and other people asked him,” confided one of Francis’ closest friends at the Vatican, Guzmán Carriquiry, the former head of the Vatican’s pontifical commission for Latin America. “But it was useless, useless! He’d respond with jokes, by staying silent or getting irritated if you insisted.” Carriquiry said Leo was coming to Argentina to “fill a void that has remained,” much in the same way Leo has undertaken trips to Spain and France — two once staunchly Christian European countries that Francis stubbornly refused to visit, preferring instead more far-flung “peripheral” places. María Marcela Mazzini, an Argentine theologian who participated in Francis’ 2015 big meeting on the family, attributed Francis’ reluctance to return to Argentina’s complicated political polarization during his pontificate. “We understand,” she said. “Things are contextual. I believe the people never doubted the pope’s affection. They always felt he was close to them and now we’re also watching with great joy as Pope Leo” continues his legacy. “So we’re waiting for him with open arms,” she said. The Argentine leg of the trip, however, is likely to be the most politically delicate, given the clear differences of priorities and styles of the reserved, pensive Leo and those of President Javier Milei, a self-described “anarcho-capitalist” who once described Francis as a “filthy leftist” and “representative of evil on Earth.” Leo Guardado, associate professor of theology at Fordham University, said he expected Milei’s push to attract AI investment and data centers to Argentina will be a point of discussion, given Leo’s concern about AI’s impact on humanity and the environment. A visit to the most secular country in Latin America The visit begins in Uruguay, the first country in the world to legalize marijuana for recreational use, the second country in Latin America to decriminalize abortion, and the third country in the Americas to legalize same-sex marriage. More recently, it became the first country in the region to approve assisted dying legislation over the strong opposition of the Catholic Church, evidence of Uruguay’s entrenched, church-state separation that prohibits any mention of God in oaths of office. “Uruguay is by far the most secularized nation in Latin America. It’s pretty much like a Western European nation,” said Andrew Chesnut, chair of Catholic studies and an expert in the Latin American church at Virginia Commonwealth University. All of which begs the question of why Leo would bother spending three days of a 12-day trip in a country of 3.5 million people, only a third of whom identify as Catholic and a fraction of whom actually goes to Mass regularly. Alvarado had a ready reply: ”Why not?” Leo is expected to make clear church teaching on abortion and euthanasia. But he is likely to also recall Uruguay’s strong Catholic roots from the Spanish colonial era, most significantly on Sunday when he marks an important Catholic feast day that is intrinsically connected to Uruguay’s 1825 declaration of independence and nationhood. “He is going to meet people and meet hearts and hopefully inspire them to look again for the places where the church was big and now is small,” Alvarado said. His message to today’s religious “nones,” or nonbelievers, is: “Reconsider.”

articles.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
articles.summary: A passenger ​plane ⁠flying from Dublin ⁠to Rome was on Thursday ⁠diverted ‌to a French air force base after a bomb ‌threat.
articles.body: LONDON — A wave of bomb threats against passenger airliners caused chaos in the skies and airports of Europe on Thursday, the latest of such incidents this week that have prompted emergency landings and security sweeps on runways. No explosives have so far been found, and it is not clear who or what is behind the security threats made against at least 14 airliners. But the threats have caused disruption to Europe’s airspace and some of its busiest airports. The threats against two flights that landed in Rome came by email that said it was made in opposition to “your feminist regime,” the airport confirmed to NBC News. Italy’s prime minister is a woman, Giorgia Meloni. One of the first reports involved Aer Lingus Flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome, which changed course near Paris and diverted to a French air force base, the airline said. There, all 151 passengers and six crewmembers were evacuated while a bomb squad inspected the aircraft, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office said in a statement. From there, reports of threats in the skies over Europe arrived at dizzying pace, triggering searches by cabin crews and then again by airport security once on the ground. Security operations were launched at airports in Prague, Copenhagen and Warsaw, with passengers at the last seeing the military and police sniffer dogs patrolling the tarmac. “It is too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked,” Apostolos Tzitzikostas, European commissioner for sustainable transport and tourism, told a news conference in Brussels, adding that “we don’t have information yet whether this is a cyber attack.” A Finnair flight from Helsinki was escorted by Italian air force jets to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport “following anonymous reports of a suspected bomb threat,” according to a spokesperson for the city’s airport authority. Bomb disposal experts found nothing. “Unfortunately, air traffic is sometimes subject to threats, as we have seen this week, when other airlines in Europe have also faced hoax bomb threats,” a Finnair spokesperson, Stiina Tuunanen, told NBC News in an email. “Threats are almost always unfounded.” That was also the case for another Finnair flight from Helsinki to Vienna, whose threat was found to be baseless after landing safely in the Austrian capital. LOT Polish Airlines said two of its aircraft from Warsaw were targeted, one flying to Brussels and the other to Paris. Back on the ground in Warsaw, Polish resident Matthew Bojarsky, 28, was about to fly to Paris for a romantic trip with his American girlfriend, but saw police, military and sniffer dogs on the tarmac, he told NBC News. Passengers were told that “safety protocols” meant their flight, LOT LO331, had to be aborted and moved to a later time. Elsewhere, three Ryanair flights were interrupted as they headed to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. Two flights, from Copenhagen and Milan, landed at their destination while a third, from London, was diverted to the city of Plovdiv, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said in an email. Ryanair did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In the Czech Republic, meanwhile, police said they had received threats about improvised explosive devices being place on four planes heading to the country’s capital, Prague. In this instance it appeared that at least some of the threats were sent by email, so “clearly there must be a process whereby airlines distinguish more credible threats from obvious hoaxes,” Peter Neumann, a professor of security studies at Kings College London, said. Thursday’s incidents follow days of airline bomb threats that have forced multiple flights to divert and an airport in Poland to briefly close. No explosive devices were found in the earlier incidents, according to authorities in various countries. On Tuesday, a security operation was also launched at the Greek island port ⁠of Syros after a bomb threat ​to an Israel-bound cruise ship. Authorities said an unknown person claimed an explosive device had been attached to ⁠the hull of the Panama-flagged Crown Iris that was due to sail ⁠to Haifa. Authorities have not indicated who could have been behind the incidents and there were no claims of responsibility.

articles.title: New bomb threats force more European flights into emergency landings
articles.summary: Flights make emergency landings in France, Italy and Bulgaria days after bomb threats disrupted air traffic.
articles.body:
Hoax bomb threats have forced more than a dozen flights to make unplanned landings across Europe, days after a ⁠⁠⁠⁠series of similar threats forced multiple flight diversions and the closure of an airport in Poland.

The warnings on Thursday affected flights between France, Italy, Bulgaria, Spain, Denmark, Poland, Romania, Ireland, the United Kingdom and the Czech Republic, among others.

An Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome was rerouted to France after a suspected bomb threat and escorted by military aircraft to the Evreux airfield west of Paris, French authorities said.

France’s air force said it scrambled planes “as soon as the threat was reported”.

The office of Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said a bomb squad was in place at the airport and that 151 passengers and six crew were moved to safety.

In a separate incident, Bulgaria reported that three aircraft had requested emergency landings on its territory due to bomb threats, according to local media.

Planes flying from Denmark’s capital, Copenhagen, and Spain’s capital, Madrid,⁠⁠ ⁠⁠landed in Sofia, the Bulgarian interior minister said, ⁠⁠⁠⁠according to broadcaster bTV.

“Upon landing, the necessary inspections were carried out in accordance with the applicable procedures and no issues were identified,” Bulgaria’s transport ministry told the Reuters news agency, adding that normal airport operations had resumed.

Meanwhile, Spanish authorities said three flights were affected by hoax bomb threats at Madrid airport. It remains unclear whether any of them were among the aircraft that made emergency landings in Sofia.

⁠Four ⁠⁠⁠⁠airplanes heading to Prague also received bomb threats. Czech police said all aircraft underwent ‌‌‌‌pyrotechnic inspections, which yielded negative results. “The investigation of the threats has been taken over by NCTEKK [the National Centre against Terrorism, Extremism and Cybercrime] and currently no further information can be provided,” it said on X.

In Belgium, ⁠⁠⁠⁠LOT Polish Airlines ⁠⁠⁠⁠said that a flight from Warsaw ⁠⁠⁠⁠to Brussels landed safely at its destination ⁠⁠⁠⁠after a security warning.

“Following receipt of information regarding ‌‌‌‌a potential security threat to flight LO235 from Warsaw to Brussels, the flight crew was notified of the situation ⁠⁠⁠⁠and conducted an onboard ⁠⁠⁠⁠inspection in accordance with established procedures. No suspicious items were ⁠⁠⁠⁠found,” a LOT spokesperson ⁠⁠⁠⁠said.

The aircraft landed ⁠⁠⁠⁠at Brussels’ Zaventem airport, where security services carried out an additional ‌‌‌‌inspection of the plane. No dangerous ‌‌‌‌or ‌‌‌‌suspicious items were found, while spokespeople for the airport said no additional ‌‌‌‌security measures were necessary.

Separately, a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw was rerouted to Vienna after a hoax bomb threat was reported, the airline said.

“The diversion was carried out in accordance with established safety protocols and procedures,” Wizz Air said in a statement.

Another hoax bomb alert was reported on a Finnair flight from Helsinki to Rome that was escorted to the Italian capital by a fighter jet and checked by bomb disposal experts, an airport spokesman told the AFP news agency.

Elsewhere, a spokesperson for the Finnish carrier said a threat was made against its Helsinki-Vienna flight operated by Jettime on Thursday. The plane landed in the Austrian capital without incident.

While no country has attributed blame for the threats, they come as many European officials are accusing Russia of planning “hybrid attacks” — often cheap, easily deniable and not expected to trigger an armed response.

Britain’s Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander told UK media that flights across Europe were hit by “malicious hoax threats.”

The European Union said it was not yet clear whether the hoax bomb alerts were connected, and that it was following events closely with national authorities.

“Any threats against civilians are unacceptable,” EU transport commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas wrote on X, adding that it was “too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked”.

The disruption comes after several European flights were targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday, prompting emergency searches, briefly shutting down an airport outside the Polish capital, Warsaw, and leading the Italian Air Force to escort a Ryanair plane into Rome.

Philip Baum, a visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University, told Al Jazeera that the number of planes forced to divert or land was “unusual”, but that “bomb threats themselves are not”.

“What has happened this week seems to be coordinated to some extent … and the authorities across multiple countries in Europe are evaluating the threat as being specific … and they demand that the aircraft actually land and be completely inspected.”

Reporting from Heathrow airport in London, Al Jazeera’s Frances Read said there was “no indication of who would be behind this, but there is a wider context in a time of geopolitical tension”.

“We’ve seen cyberattacks on other things, like a hack on supermarket refrigerators which turned up the temperature to spoil food in supermarkets across Europe, and we’ve seen drone incursions as well,” the correspondent said.

The German government has blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport in August.

While there is no evidence linking the recent bomb threats to these previous attacks, “that is realistically what European governments will be looking at,” Read added.

articles.title: US sanctions Indian and Turkish firms accused of helping Iran
articles.summary: US Treasury says Indian couple faked ship registries for countries including Guyana and Laos to help Iranian tankers.
articles.body:
The United States has imposed sanctions on companies and individuals in India and Turkiye that it accuses of helping Iran get around restrictions on its oil exports and its airlines.

The US Department of the Treasury said on Wednesday that the measures target a “vast criminal network” run by Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, who are based in the northern Indian city of Chandigarh.

Two other Indian nationals who head the couple’s businesses and nine entities linked to Sharma were also sanctioned.

According to the Treasury, the couple falsely claimed to represent the maritime authorities of countries including Guyana, Eswatini and Laos. It said they issued fake flags and certifications that allowed sanctioned tankers carrying Iranian oil to continue operating, including vessels working for the Iranian military and its allied groups.

The department said the scheme dated back to at least 2014 and relied on websites built to resemble official national ship registries.

The Treasury also sanctioned Turkiye-based Fugo Ground Services. It said the company provided ground handling and other services to several US-sanctioned Iranian airlines that still fly to Turkiye, including Iran Air Tour and Saha Airlines.

The Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control also warned shipping companies about the sanctions risks of dealing with vessels sailing under false flags.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington would continue to pursue anyone who supports Tehran.

The sanctions freeze any US assets held by those targeted and generally bar Americans from dealing with them.

The measures are part of the Trump administration’s “Operation Economic Outcast”, which aims to cut off oil revenue Iran uses to fund its war effort. The Treasury said last week that its campaign had pushed Iran’s currency, the rial, to new lows and driven inflation to about 90 percent.

The sanctions were announced a day after Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in US midterm elections.

articles.title: ‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday reiterated her commitment to return to Dhaka in December despite a death sentence
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday reiterated her commitment to return to Dhaka in December despite a death sentence awaiting her return from India.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told The Associated Press in response to questions by email.“So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed,” Hasina said.The former leader has served as Prime Minister of Bangladesh for one term from 1996 to 2001 and four consecutive terms from 2009 to 2024.In 2024, Hasina sought asylum in New Delhi after a mass student-led uprising overthrew her government. In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal ordered her death sentence for crimes against humanity. She was tried for ordering a crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to the United Nations data, cited by AP, nearly 1,400 were killed during the unrest.The former PM has denied wrongdoing, rejected the tribunal's verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India to extradite her. However, New Delhi said the request was being legally examined.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” India’s high commissioner to Dhaka Dinesh Trivedi remarked during an October discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.On Wednesday, Hasina told the AP that she was aware of the risks she could face on returning, but had no intention of changing her decision.“I know that I may be arrested when I return. I may be imprisoned, tortured or even killed. I am fully aware of those possibilities. But I cannot spend the rest of my life watching my people suffer from a distance,” she told the news agency.Hasina did not specify how she intended to travel back to Bangladesh from India.Hasina alleges crackdown on Awami League membersHer proposed return comes as her Awami League party faces an uncertain political future. The party remains banned, while several of its senior leaders have been arrested or forced into exile.Hasina alleged that at least 20,000 party members had been killed since August 2024. She also claimed that thousands had been arrested, tortured or driven into hiding, while supporters had lost their homes, businesses and livelihoods because of their political affiliations.“There is no normal political or democratic environment,” she said, accusing the authorities of systematically targeting the party.Following Hasina's removal from office, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus headed an interim administration for 18 months. In February, Tarique Rahman, son of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and a longstanding political rival of Hasina, won a landslide victory in an election held under the interim government. The Awami League was barred from contesting the polls.Several rights organisations, including Human Rights Watch, have criticised Rahman's government over alleged violations of civil and political rights in recent months. The government has maintained that arrests have been made in connection with specific charges.Hasina raises concern over influence of extremist groupsHasina also expressed concern over the growing influence of hard-line groups in Bangladesh, saying the political climate had allowed extremist elements to gain confidence.“The present political environment has allowed extremist elements to become more confident,” she said.Global rights groups and independent observers had earlier raised concerns about radical groups seeking to suppress liberal forces during the Yunus-led interim administration. Minority communities have also reported facing intimidation.The interim government denied the allegations. The current administration has continued to face criticism over the deteriorating law and order situation in the country.Hasina, who took a tough stance against radical groups during her 15 years in power, said she was worried about their growing influence.Asked whether she expected countries such as the United States and India to press Bangladesh to ensure her safe return, Hasina said she was not seeking protection from foreign governments.“I value friendship and cooperation with all nations. That has always been our (Bangladesh's) foreign policy. But I do not need the blessing of a foreign power to return to my own country,” she said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Married at First Sight UK cancelled after BBC revealed rape allegations
articles.summary: Channel 4 will reinvest the show's budget in "distinctive new programming" and said sorry again to the women involved.
articles.body:
Married at First Sight UK will not return, Channel 4 has said, following a BBC investigation into the hit reality TV show.

The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis earlier this year, after Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show , while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.

A review was commissioned by Channel 4 shortly after the BBC first contacted the broadcaster, with details of the allegations we had heard.

On Thursday, the completed review recommended extra safeguards on the show. But Channel 4 said the programme had "run its course" and apologised to the women involved in the investigation.

The broadcaster's chief executive Priya Dogra said she was "very sorry for the distress those women have clearly felt", adding that the show's budget would be reinvested in "distinctive new programming".

The Panorama investigation in May, in which three women made allegations about the men they were partnered with - claims the men deny, made the following allegations:

One woman said her onscreen husband raped her and threatened her with an acid attack.

A second woman told both Channel 4 and CPL, before broadcast, about being allegedly raped by her onscreen husband. Her episodes were still aired.

A third woman - Shona Manderson, the only woman who was identified - accused her onscreen husband of sexual misconduct.

All three women accused the show of not doing enough to protect them.

Lawyers for CPL, the independent production company that makes the UK version of the show, previously said its welfare system is "gold standard" and industry-leading, and that it acted appropriately in all these cases.

Channel 4 had initially told Panorama that all the allegations were "wholly uncorroborated".

Dame Caroline Dinenage MP, chair of the House of Commons culture and media committee, said the decision to axe the show "makes sense" given the review's findings and the "seriousness of the allegations".

"Reality TV contestants have often been treated as a commodity, with duty of care a slogan rather than a genuine principle. Everyone involved in producing and regulating reality TV must now learn and act," she added.

A spokesman for Ofcom said the broadcast regulator would "carefully consider the reports published today as we move to strengthen our guidance for broadcasters".

"We are clear that broadcasters have a duty of care towards members of the public who participate in their programmes."

The review into the show was split into two - one part examined welfare protocols on MAFS UK, and the other reported on how Channel 4 handled the allegations.

The review into welfare protocols, led by former BBC One Controller Lorraine Heggessey, concluded that some parts of the programme's format increased "the risk profile of the show".

Although she found the protocols for MAFS UK were extremely thorough and of a high standard, she said "intimacy is a key focus", and that "some elements of the show could implicitly put pressure on contributors to be intimate".

Heggessey made suggestions including installing CCTV in all areas of the apartments, constantly monitored by a welfare team, with panic buttons and "safe words" in place.

She concluded that, with enhancements to the existing welfare framework and adjustments to the format, it would have been reasonable to continue to produce future series of MAFS UK.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's PM programme on Thursday, she added that the suggested changes "would have, in lots of ways, changed both the format and the nature of the show, but would have given the kind of protection that both Channel Four and CPL would have ideally looked for to ensure the safety of all contributors".

But she added that she "completely understood" why Dogra "decided that she doesn't want to proceed with it".

The other part of the review, by law firm Clyde & Co, found that Channel 4 and CPL's welfare protocols were compliant with Ofcom's broadcasting code.

There were no findings of a breach of the code regarding the handling of issues raised at the relevant times.

But it said there were "a small number of instances" where the show's protocols had not been fully applied.

This included one incident when "some contributors contravened the Code of Conduct relating to prohibited substances but were given a first and final warning rather than being removed from the programme".

It added that Channel 4 and CPL could have undertaken a more structured longer-term review over multiple series.

The review also made recommendations for areas where the contributor welfare framework could be "further strengthened".

Dogra said welfare across all of their programmes is "a primary concern".

She said that considering the "wholesale implementation" of the recommendations "provoked fundamental questions about the editorial proposition of a show that, I believe, has now run its course over 10 years".

She added that the review "did not have the authority to adjudicate on the very serious allegations made by three women in the Panorama programme".

Billed as a "bold social experiment", Married at First Sight UK - known to many as MAFS - sees single people agree to "marry" total strangers, after meeting for the first time at their mock weddings.

The marriages are not legally binding, but viewers see the couples go on honeymoon, before moving in together and navigating their relationships - all while being filmed, almost every day.

The UK version, which had been running for 10 seasons, is one of Channel 4's biggest shows, with audience figures often topping three million.

Following the Panorama broadcast, Channel 4's chief executive Priya Dogra initially didn't apologise, although she did express her "sympathy" for those who had spoken up.

Less than 48 hours later, she changed position, telling reporters she was "deeply sorry" over the women's distress.

The impact of the Panorama progamme was swift, and sizeable.

Channel 4 launched its external review, all the episodes were taken down from its streaming service, and a major sponsor pulled out .

Married at First Sight UK usually starts airing in September, but the new series was put on hold following the revelations in the Panorama.

Ofcom has since launched an investigation, and in June, a male cast member was arrested on suspicion of rape .

The individual is not being named. The alleged victim is also not being named; anyone who makes an allegation of rape is entitled to anonymity by law.

If you have more information about this story, you can reach Noor by email at noor.nanji@bbc.co.uk
